newsitem.title: USA: USDA says almost 20 mln acres offered for CRP.
newsitem.headline: USDA says almost 20 mln acres offered for CRP.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Tuesday said almost 20 million acres had been offered for enrollment in the new Conservation Reserve Program at the end of the third week of sign-up for the program.

USDA said of the nearly 20 million acres offered, about 14.7 million acres are currently enrolled under CRP contracts due to expire in September and about 5.3 million acres are new and were offered for the first time.

"All indications from the field are that CRP sign-up is going very well," Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said in a statement. "I am delighted at the response we've been getting from farmers and ranchers and other landowners all across the country."
Sign-up for the revampled land-idling program began March 3 and closes March 28. USDA said producers will be notified by mid-June what acres have been accepted into CRP.
Texas has the largest number of acres offered, with nearly 2.5 million acres, followed by 2.0 million acres in Montana and 1.9 million acres in North Dakota, the department said.
